caseno:
Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6544 of 2000 
with Criminal Revision No. 578 of 2000
lawyer:
Md Mahbub Ali with Reba Kaniz, Advocates ----- For Petitioner. [In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6544/2000]
Abdus Salam Mamun, Advocate  ----- For the Petitioner. [In Criminal Rev. Case No. 578 of 2000] 
M Farooq, Deputy Attorney-General with Shueb Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General  ----- For the State.
parties:
Tajul Islam  ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Gobinda Prashad Das and others ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Md Ali Asgar Khan J : Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6544 of 2000 and Criminal Revision No. 578 of 2000 arises out of the same proceeding in Special Case No. 213 of 1999, pending before the Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong Division, Chittagong and therefore, these two Rules are taken up together for hearing and this judgment will govern both the Rules. 

 2. The short facts for the purpose of disposal of the Rules is that, opposite party No. 1 as complainant filed a petition of complaint before the Senior Special Judge, Cox's Bazar alleging, inter alia, that on 29-12-91 he went to the Court of Thana Magistrate, Chokoria for inquiry about the next date and position of GR Case No. 25 of 1991 and Chokoria PS Case No. 14(9) of 1991 instituted by his father and requested the accused No.1 for giving such information who on reply told that previously his father used to take such information without giving any tips to them and this time if he wants any information then he shall have to pay Taka 500 or else asked him to get out of the office telling him that without making such payment no information will be supplied. When he protested this act on the part of the accused No. 1 Tarani Mohan Ghosh, the accused No.3 Abu Zafa directed the accused No. 2 Tajul Islam to snatch away money from him and after getting such direction of accused No. 3, the accused No. 2 snatched away money from him and after getting such direction of accused No. 3, the accused No.2 snatched away Taka 300 from his pocket which the accused No. 2 gave to accused No. 1 Tarani Mohan Ghosh as illegal grantification. At that time, the persons present protested this sort of behaviour meted out to him by the accused when the accused No. 2 at the order of accused Nos. 1 and 3 put him in court hazat after assaulting him by fists and blows. He cried out when he was put inside the court hazat which drew the attention of some of the persons present there who went to the house of his sister and brought Taka 500 which was given to the accused No.1 as illegal gratification who accepted the same on behalf of all accused. After realising illegal gratifications from him the accused persons talked among themselves that if he was released from court hazat then there is every possibility of filing a case by him against them and due to such apprehension the accused No.1 filed a false case against him under section 353 of the Penal Code being GR Case No. 205 of 1991. The accused petitioners with a view to realise illegal gratification illegally detained him in the Court hajat and realised illegal gratification by physical and mental torture and kept him confined in the Court hazat on the basis of false allegations till 31-12-91 when he was released therefrom on making payment of illegal gratification and thereby, the accused petitioners committed an offence under sections 161/323/342/352 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. 

 3. The learned Special Judge, Cox's Bazar after receipt of the complaint petition sent the same to the District Anti-Corruption Officer, Cox's Bazar for inquiry and report against which accused No. 1 Tarani Mohan Ghosh preferred Criminal Revision being No. 754 of 1995 which was made absolute with a direction to the Special Judge, Cox's Bazar to proceed with the case as provided under section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 and accordingly, the learned Special Judge took cognizance of the case against the accused petitioners after seeking permission for according sanction and after expiry of 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of such letter as required. Thereafter, the learned Special Judge, Cox's Bazar sent back the case to the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong Division, Chittagong for trial where Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong Division, Chittagong framed charge against the accused petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 after rejecting the application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Against this order of the learned Divisional Special Judge of framing charge, the accused petitioners moved this court with the present applications and obtained the Rule. 

 4. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that there is no ingredients of sections 161/342 of the Penal Code for framing charge against the accused petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code and, as such, framing of charge is illegal and therefor, the impugned order and the proceeding of Special Case No. 213 of 1999 is liable to be quashed. He further submits that the learned Divisional Special Judge committed an illegality in framing charge of non-schedule offence with the schedule offence and that this violation of law also renders the framing of charge against the accused petitioners illegal for which the proceeding in question should be quashed. In support of his contention, he has cited two decisions in the case of Dalpat Singh and another vs State of Rajasthan reported in 1969 Criminal Law Journal 262 (Vol. 75 CN 64); AIR 1969 Supreme Court 17(V 56C-7) and Abdul Gani, vs State reported in 24 DLR 230 (162). 

 5. The learned Deputy Attorney-General opposes the Rules stating that the allegations as made in the petition of complaint disclosed an offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and, as such, the learned Divisional Special Judge committed no illegality in framing charge against the accused petitioners for which the same is not liable to be quashed. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that in respect of allegation of accused petitioner Abu Zafar it clearly discloses an offence of abetment as alleged in the petition of complaint and therefore, it cannot be said that he did not commit any offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code. In support of his contention he cited the decision in the case of Hussain Mohammad Ershad vs State, reported in 45 DLR (AD) 48. 

 7. We have perused the petition including the petition of complaint, the impugned order and other materials on record. In the petition of complaint, it is alleged that the accused petitioners in collusion with each other demanded illegal gratification from the complainant when he went to the Court of Thana Magistrate, Chakoria for getting information as to the next date of GR case No. 25 of 1991 and PS case No. 14(9)91 and that on his refusal to pay such illegal gratification at the order of accused No.3 the accused No. 2 snatched away Taka 300 from his pocket and physically assaulted him. It is also alleged that the accused petitioners being apprehensive of any action to be taken by the complainant for assaulting him and subsequently the accused No. 1 filed a case against the complainant making false allegation. It is also alleged that on getting this information his sister came with Taka 500 and after giving the illegal gratification requested the accused petitioners to release the complainant from the Court hajat but it was turned down and subsequently implicated him falsely in a case with apprehension that he will file a case against them. On receipt of the complaint the learned Special Judge sent the case to the District Anti-Corruption Officer for inquiry and report who submitted a report on being found prima facie case against the petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. Against this accused No.1 Tarani Mohan Ghosh filed Criminal Revision being 754 of 1995 which was made absolute with a direction to the Special Judge for prosecuting the said case being Special Case No. 213 of 1999 after obtaining necessary sanction from the relevant authority as required under section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The learned Special Judge, Cox's Bazar accordingly, as it appears, wrote to the government for according sanction for prosecution of the accused petitioners in this case and after expiry of the period as stipulated he took cognizance of the offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. The learned Special Judge, Cox's Bazar thereafter, transferred the case to the Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong Division, Chittagong. The learned Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong Division, Chittagong on consideration of the allegations as made in the petition of complaint including the police report and other materials on record framed charge against the accused petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 rejecting the prayer of the accused petitioners under section 241A of the CrPC as prima facie case was proved against the accused petitioners for the offence alleged to have been committed by them. The learned Divisional Special Judge as it appears rejected the petition on finding that the allegation as made in the petition of complaint discloses an offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and accordingly, framed charge. The learned Divisional Special Judge in rejecting the prayer of the accused petitioners observed that there is no substance in the submission that there is no ingredients of the offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code as alleged in the petition of complaint and that the allegation prima facie discloses an offence against the accused petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 and therefore, framed charge after rejecting the prayer of accused petitioners under section 241A of the CrPC. In rejecting the prayer the learned Divisional Special Judge also observed that the accused petitioners are also liable to be tried in respect of the non-schedule offence under section 342 of the Penal Code along with section 161 of the Penal Code which is the schedule offence as the offence was committed in course of the same transaction and, as such, there is no legal bar for continuing the trial of the case along with section 161 of the Penal Code which is the schedule offence under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 8. We have also perused the petition of complaint including the impugned order of the learned Divisional Special Judge. The allegation as disclosed in the petition of complaint prima facie shows that there are ingredients of the offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code as the accused petitioners in collusion with each other demanded illegal gratification from the complainant for giving him information regarding the date and position of the GR and PS cases filed by the father of the complainant and when the complainant refused to comply with such illegal demand, the accused petitioners in collusion with each other snatched away Taka 300 from his pocket. It also appears that subsequently, the accused petitioners realised Taka 500 as illegal gratification from the complainant when he was put into court hajat immediately after the occurrence upon assaulting him. So, the complaint petition as it appears prima facie discloses an offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code. 

 9. The contention of the learned Advocate that since admittedly the complainant was put into custody in connection with a case, so section 342 of the Penal Code has no manner of application in this case is of no substance, since it is alleged in the complaint petition that when there was a hue and cry and the witnesses assembled there, the accused petitioners illegally put him in Court hajat and thereafter manufactured a case. The accused No. 1 Tarani Mohan Ghosh lodged the case against the complainant in the Chakoria Thana which is not compoundable. Since, the case was started in the Thana in the court compound, so it is apparent that the FIR was lodged subsequently after taking the complainant in the court hajat and it further supports the case of the complainant in that in the FIR lodged by the accused No. 1 there is no allegation that the FIR was lodged on production of the complainant with the police. From this it is apparent that the complainant was first put in court hajat and thereafter the case was filed and therefore an offence under section 342 of the Penal Code is disclosed. The accused petitioner by using their official power and position filed the case after putting the complainant in court hazat which is apparent from the fact and circumstances of the case and also the allegations made in the complaint petition. The learned Divisional Special Judge also appears to have rejected the petition under section 241A of the CrPC in considering all these aspects of the case and the allegations made in the petition of complaint and framed charge against the accused petitioners for the offence alleged to have been committed by them under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. 

 10. As regards the submission of the learned Advocate that no offence is disclosed against the accused petitioner Abu Jafar under section 161 of the Penal Code does not stand in view of the facts and circumstances of the case. On perusal of the complaint petition and other materials on record, we find that he committed an offence under section 161 of the Penal Code as in the complaint petition it is also alleged that after the complainant was put into court hajat all the accused persons realised Taka 500 from the complaint's sister as illegal gratification and therefore, it cannot be said that no offence under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code is disclosed against this petitioner. 

 11. The decisions as referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioners have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case as the cited decisions were in respect of the accused persons who preferred appeal against conviction and which were decided on merits but the instant case is under trial and whether there is legal offence or not under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code is a matter to be decided at the time of trial and, as such, the decisions as referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioners are not applicable in this case. 

 12. The decision as referred to by the learned Deputy Attorney-General as regards abetment of accused petitioner Abu Jafar is quite applicable in view of the facts and circumstances of the present case as it was decided that abetment is an offence under the Penal Code and a person may be charged for abetting an offence made punishable by a Special Act even though abetment may not have been mentioned as an offence under the Special Act and, as such, the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that no offence lies against the accused petitioner Abu Jafar is of no avail. 

 13. In this view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the allegations made in the petition of complaint it cannot be said that no offence is disclosed against the accused petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. On the contrary, we find that the complaint petition discloses an offence against the accused petitioners under sections 161/342 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. Therefore, it cannot be said that no offence has been committed by the accused petitioners as alleged. Further, it appears that the allegations in this case was made against the accused petitioners who are police officials and which are normally unusual and, as such, we consider that the allegations against the accused petitioners should be inquired into in the trial. 

 14. In the above facts and circumstances of the case, we do not find any ground to interfere with the proceedings in Special Case No. 213 of 1999, pending before the Divisional Special Judge, Chittagong Division, Chittagong and, as such, the Rules are liable to be discharged.
